prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (Z2 classification), and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B038 as my preferred single-part configuration, but with a narrower public position than in round 1. The achievement is a new classification of insulators by a Z2 invariant protected by time-reversal symmetry, giving helical edge channels that follow from symmetry rather than from material detail. Kane and Mele supplied the invariant and the quantum spin Hall prediction; Molenkamp's group observed the nonlocal, quantised edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells. The concept has since been confirmed independently in several platforms (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, and by ARPES in Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3), and it now organises how band structures are searched for. It is about two decades old, so maturity is not the issue. The chair's questions have sharpened what I am actually claiming. I now word the citation strictly around the prediction of the effect and the first observation, so it makes no claim on the HgTe proposal or on the 3D topological insulators. Within that scope, Kane-Mele's theory and Molenkamp's observation are each decisive and independently identifiable, and three names map onto one prediction and one observation. My preference rests on judging a new organising principle that survives across materials above a record-setting instrument. That is a judgement about what the prize should reward, not an objective ranking, and I do not count the tally in B038's favour.
statement.case_against: The credit chain is still not clean. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe realisation that Molenkamp tested, and the 3D theory and ARPES work (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Hsieh-Hasan) lie outside the three names, so a narrow citation answers the charge of overclaiming but not the charge of an incomplete story. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and topological phases will make some members see this as a continuation, and I have not shown that to be wrong, only that the Z2 time-reversal-invariant case is a distinct classification. Round 1 also sharpened a weakness in my own argument: Kroll and Lindroth are right that neither the 2005 nor the 2012 prize contains the magic-wavelength idea. I therefore cannot present B046 as an instrument refinement of recognised work, and my case for B038 over B046 reduces to a preference for concept over instrument. The practical payoff of B038, dissipationless edge transport, has also not materialised.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the 2005 and 2012 prizes honoured the comb and single-ion control but not the magic-wavelength idea, which removes the light shift while keeping many atoms, and that B046 has the cleanest attribution on the list.
responses.response: This weakens my round-1 argument and I accept the correction. I had treated B046 as a refinement of an already honoured line, but the magic-wavelength lattice is a separate idea, and the 1e-18 agreement between independent laboratories is as strong a form of verification as an experiment can have. I also agree with you and Eva Lindroth that the prize should not wait for the redefinition of the second, which would make our judgement depend on another body's schedule. My remaining difference is the discovery-versus-instrument distinction you draw yourself: B038 changed what physicists look for in materials, whereas B046 changed what can be measured. I do not think the committee must resolve that in B038's favour, and I record B046 as my first alternative, one I would accept without reservation about its merit.

responses.point: Pearce prefers B046 for a clean two-name attribution that B038 lacks, and the chair's summary asks whether a prediction-plus-first-observation citation avoids the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap.
responses.response: Your attribution point is the strongest argument against my position, and I do not think a citation fully removes it. Narrow wording, 'the prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and its first observation in HgTe quantum wells', keeps us from claiming that Kane, Mele and Molenkamp originated the HgTe proposal. But the committee would still be choosing which incomplete story to tell. Where I differ is on weight: B046 leaves out Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto and the Paris and PTB groups, so it also carries an attribution question, a different one in kind. I do not claim B038 is cleaner than B046 on credit. My claim is that its credit gap is bounded and can be stated in a citation, while its concept is broader.

responses.point: Danielsson moved to B038 partly because of its breadth of cross-member support and wants the citation worded around the prediction and first observation so that it does not claim the HgTe proposal.
responses.response: I agree on the wording and have adopted it in my citation. I would add a caution about the support argument: B038's high opening ranks do not settle the scientific case and should not carry weight in the vote. Round 1 shows the committee is split on the substance, with five members on B046, so the case must stand on the physics. I also disagree with your description of the HgTe proposal as a background wrinkle. Molenkamp's experiment was designed around it, which is why the committee should say openly in its public explanation that the proposal is outside the citation and that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's contribution is acknowledged, rather than implying the chain is complete.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the 2016 prize concerned topological phase transitions and integer quantum Hall physics, so that time-reversal-invariant Kane-Mele physics is distinct, but she also treats the incomplete credit as the real obstacle for B038 and would not wait for the redefinition of the second for B046.
responses.response: I agree with you on both halves. The 2016 prize rewarded topology in the presence of a magnetic field and broken time-reversal symmetry. B038 is the class protected by time-reversal symmetry with spin-orbit coupling, so it extends the topological idea rather than repeating it, though the overlap is a fair concern for others on the committee. I agree that the incomplete credit chain is the obstacle. Since you also say the redefinition of the second need not be awaited, I note that the timing argument against B046 has largely been withdrawn in this round, and I cannot rely on it to rank B038 above the clock.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B042 as a falsifiable flat-band prediction confirmed by experiment, rests the citation on flat bands and observed correlated states rather than the pairing mechanism, and notes that the field is reproduced across groups and material families.
responses.response: Your framing of the citation is sound and answers part of my round-1 objection, since a prize need not explain the superconductivity. The prediction-then-experiment structure is also the same one B038 has. My remaining difficulty with B042 is that this is a discovery of a platform whose phase diagram is still sample-dependent, with Cao, Fatemi and the earlier continuum-model authors outside the three names. B038 has two decades of confirmation across several materials and B042 has eight years. I keep B042 as an alternative and would reassess it in a few years, but I do not consider it premature as a scientific result.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can defend omitting Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang from a B038 prize, even with a citation limited to the prediction of the effect and its first observation. I do not think this is resolved.
Whether the prize should cover only the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or also the 3D topological insulators, which would involve names outside the credited set. I would keep it to 2D.
How much distance the 2016 prize leaves. I regard Z2 time-reversal-invariant classification as distinct, but this is a judgement others dispute.

Whether my preference for a concept over an instrument is the right criterion, given that the magic-wavelength insight in B046 is a concept too and no longer falls under the 2005 and 2012 prizes. I hold this view with less confidence than in round 1.
I am recalling priority details (Kane-Mele 2005, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang 2006, Konig et al. 2007) from memory and have not verified them against the supplied record.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen from the first round and none is documented for B038, B046 or B042. None of the credited names for these entries appears among my documented co-authors, supervisors or institutions, and my work on stochastic processes, turbulence and neural networks is not close to any shortlisted topic. The chair's flags concern other members' proximity to B006 and B046, and I raise no objection to their participation as long as they disclose it.
